dedupe_keys.name: google smartphone decimeter challenge android raw gnss measurement datasets

description: Google publishes datasets of raw satellite navigation measurements recorded by Android phones during drives, with high-accuracy ground truth, first for the Google Smartphone Decimeter Challenge held with the Institute of Navigation's GNSS+ conference in 2021 and in later editions. The phones log raw GNSS observations through the Android API: carrier-to-noise density, pseudoranges from satellite transmit and signal arrival times, carrier phase and Doppler, on L1 and L5 signals from GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou and QZSS, together with phone sensors; ground truth comes from a NovAtel SPAN GNSS and inertial system in the same vehicle. The first release has 39 traces collected with Pixel 4, Pixel 4 XL and Xiaomi Mi 8 phones, mostly in California, and competitors tried to reach decimetre-level positioning with smartphones. Data were collected by Google staff on Google phones in public areas. Coverage: mainly the San Francisco Bay Area and other US roads, 2020 onward. Format and access: CSV and text logs on Kaggle, free after accepting Kaggle and competition terms. Caveats: a few phone models and regions; urban canyons are under-represented in early releases. Simulation uses: benchmarking positioning algorithms, calibrating error models for smartphone GNSS under multipath and interference, and testing spoofing and jamming detectors. Related records: the Fraunhofer, Jammertest and OAKBAT data cover interference, and the IGS products give precise orbits.
